messages:
sam: Hi team — Acquaria reached out: webhooks started failing right after the maintenance window. They say our requests are hitting IPs not on their allowlist. Can someone confirm if we rotated egress for vpc-prod-2?

egress-bot: Completed NAT reassign for vpc-prod-2 at 1919999900. Rotated pool -> 198.51.100.128/28 (old: 203.0.113.32/28). rotation_id=rot-2026-03-17-07

ingrid: Looking at our NAT logs now — I see a mix. Majority came from new pool 198.51.100.128/28 but about ~12% of flows still used addresses in 203.0.113.32/28 (203.0.113.45, 203.0.113.46). That suggests sticky SNAT or connection reuse during the handover.

alex: Can we get a failing curl from the customer (they said 403). Also need the exact webhook host they call and a sample timestamp so we can match logs.

sam: Customer pasted this quick repro (they're behind corp firewall):

```
$ curl -v https://hooks.acquaria.example.com/api/receive -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"event":"ping"}'
*   Trying 198.51.100.130:443...
* Connected to hooks.acquaria.example.com (198.51.100.130) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
> POST /api/receive HTTP/1.1
> Host: hooks.acquaria.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.85.0
> Content-Type: application/json
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ "error": "source IP not allowlisted" }
```

They also attached a firewall ingress log showing a rejected connection from 203.0.113.45 at 2026-03-17T07:12:03Z.

julia: Two things likely combined: our egress rotation + the customer's firewall that resolves the webhook hostname and allows by IP at lookup time but caches DNS results (their TTL is 3600). If the firewall resolved earlier and cached the old block, then connections that hit old IPs will be blocked.

ingrid: Confirming: we rotated the pool, but because some clients (long-lived outbound connections from our infra) maintained the previous SNAT mapping for a short window, a fraction of requests used old addresses. Also noticed a misconfigured route-map in AZ-b where SNAT table didn't flush immediately — I've attached the snippet:

```
NAT Table vpc-prod-2 AZ-b
src 10.12.4.0/24 -> snat 203.0.113.32-203.0.113.47 (sticky timeout 86400)
post-rotate rule missing update -> fallback uses old pool for established flows
```

alex: Short-term mitigation: we can pin the customer's VPC to a sticky SNAT from the new pool or temporarily re-enable the old pool while they update their allowlist. Which is less risky?

sam: Customer is OK with a short pin while they update. They asked for the list of IPs to add plus repro steps to validate.

ingrid: I can pin them to the new pool for 24h via policy flag `egress.pin.acquaria=true` — that will force SNAT to 198.51.100.128/28 for all flows from acq-1234. Applying now.

egress-bot: Policy apply accepted. acq-1234 pinned to 198.51.100.128/28 until 1920004199.

julia: Follow-up guidance for customer: 1) Add both current and previous pools to allowlist while they update DNS caching, i.e. 198.51.100.128/28 and 203.0.113.32/28. 2) Reduce DNS TTL on their firewall or switch to allowlists by CIDR rather than hostname resolution. 3) Consider webhook-level auth (HMAC or mTLS) so firewall rules aren't the only auth layer.

sam: Draft message I'll send to Acquaria (cc'ing network contacts):

"Thanks — we rotated your egress pool as part of maintenance. Short term we've pinned you to the new pool 198.51.100.128/28 for 24h while you update your allowlist. Please add both 198.51.100.128/28 and 203.0.113.32/28, and share a sample rejected line from your firewall logs if issues persist. If you can reduce DNS TTL, that will avoid cache-based mismatches next time. We'll follow up with a post-mortem once we confirm stability."

alex: Good. After they confirm, we should audit the route-map and the automation that updates SNAT entries to ensure no AZ-specific stale configs. Also add an alert if >5% of flows use the previous pool for >5m after a rotation.

ingrid: Agreed — filing infra ticket to tighten post-rotate flush and add the alert. Ticket: INFRA-3742.

julia: Thanks everyone. Sam, please keep thread updated when Acquaria confirms allowlist change. Closing for now but will reopen if customer still sees rejects. :white_check_mark:
